questions.question: When ذُو الْحَال is a نَكِرَة, why does حَال precede it in the sentence?
options: To signal that the sentence carries a negative meaning
To prevent confusion with a مَوْصُوف-صِفَة (described noun + adjective) construction
Because حَال must always be مَنْصُوب in this configuration
Because نَكِرَة words cannot be followed by حَال
questions.explanation: When ذو الحال is نَكِرَة, placing Hal after it would look identical to a Mawsuf-Sifah construction. Moving Hal first removes this ambiguity.

questions.question: What type of ambiguity does تَمْيِيز specifically resolve?
options: Ambiguity about who the subject of a sentence is
Ambiguity about the case of a pronoun after a preposition
إِبْهَام (ambiguity) in quantity, weight, volume, or area
Gender or number disagreement between a noun and its adjective
questions.explanation: تَمْيِيز is a نَكِرَة مَنْصُوب that removes إِبْهَام — ambiguity specifically related to quantity, weight, volume, or area.

questions.question: In a كَلَام مُوجَب (affirmative sentence), what case must الْمُسْتَثْنَى take?
options: It is مَرْفُوع when the مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ is the subject
It is always مَجْرُور because إِلَّا acts like a preposition
It takes the same case as the مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ
It is obligatorily مَنْصُوب
questions.explanation: In an affirmative sentence (كَلَام مُوجَب), الْمُسْتَثْنَى is obligatorily مَنْصُوب. Only in a negative sentence with مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ present may it alternatively be parsed as a بَدَل.

questions.question: What is تَمْيِيز?
options: A noun after إِلَّا that is excluded from the ruling
A definite noun that describes the state of the subject
A نَكِرَة مَنْصُوب that removes ambiguity in quantity or measure
The word or sentence whose ambiguity Tamiz resolves
questions.explanation: تَمْيِيز is defined as a نَكِرَة مَنْصُوب that resolves إِبْهَام — specifically the kind found in quantity, weight, volume, or area expressions.

questions.question: What does مُتَّصِل mean when describing الْمُسْتَثْنَى?
options: The exception belongs to a different category than the مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ
The exception must be مَنْصُوب in all sentence types
The exception occurs in an affirmative sentence
The exception belongs to the same category as the مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ
questions.explanation: مُتَّصِل (connected) means the excepted noun comes from the same category as the مُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ, as opposed to مُنْقَطِع (disconnected), where it belongs to a different category.

questions.question: What were the two specific prohibitions in Allah's مِيثَاق with Bani Isra'il in Al-Baqarah 84–86?
options: Do not ally with pagan tribes, and do not leave the land of Canaan
Do not worship idols, and do not steal from one another
Do not kill one another, and do not expel one another from your homes
Do not break the Sabbath, and do not follow other prophets
questions.explanation: Allah's covenant with Bani Isra'il contained two clear prohibitions: do not kill each other, and do not drive each other out of your homes — both of which they knowingly violated.

questions.question: Why did Bani Isra'il fight against their own Jewish brothers despite knowing it was forbidden by the Torah?
options: They believed their brothers had abandoned the Torah entirely
They were honoring tribal alliances with the Aws and Khazraj
They sought to seize the properties of expelled families
They were ordered to do so by a foreign king
questions.explanation: Bani Isra'il sided with their Arab tribal allies (Aws and Khazraj) against fellow Jews, then — contradicting themselves — cited the Torah to justify ransoming the very captives they helped create.

questions.question: What does the Quranic rhetorical question أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ establish about selective scripture-following?
options: Partial belief is still rewarded as long as core tenets are accepted
The condemnation applies only to those who deny scripture verbally
A believer may follow easier rulings when circumstances are difficult
Believing in part of scripture while rejecting other parts constitutes disbelief in the whole Book
questions.explanation: The verse condemns Bani Isra'il for honoring the ransom ruling while ignoring the prohibition on killing and expulsion — establishing that selective scripture-following amounts to rejecting the whole Book.

questions.question: What is a مِيثَاق?
options: A simple verbal promise between two individuals
A recommended act of worship recorded in the Torah
A divine punishment sent upon those who disobey
A firm, confirmed covenant — stronger than a simple promise
questions.explanation: مِيثَاق denotes a weighty, confirmed covenant — a stronger bond than an ordinary promise (وَعْد), indicating the solemnity of the obligation placed on Bani Isra'il.

questions.question: Which term refers to captives of war in the Quranic passage?
options: تُفَادُوهُمْ
خِزْي
أُسَارَى
إِجْلَاء
questions.explanation: أُسَارَى means captives of war. The passage highlights Bani Isra'il ransoming (تُفَادُوهُمْ) these captives while having first helped cause their capture.

questions.question: According to Hanafi fiqh, what immediately ends a traveler's entitlement to pray Qasr?
options: Reaching a destination that is 15 days' travel from home
Completing the stated purpose of one's journey
Returning to any city where the traveler previously lived for a year
Entering one's وَطَن أَصْلِي (primary homeland)
questions.explanation: Entering the وَطَن أَصْلِي ends Qasr immediately. Returning to a former city one has permanently migrated away from does not — as demonstrated by the Prophet ﷺ praying Qasr in Makkah after settling in Madinah.

questions.question: A person missed a prayer while traveling. How must that prayer be made up (قَضَاء)?
options: As two rak'at, because it was missed in a state of travel
As four rak'at if the person is now a resident when making it up
As two or four rak'at at the person's own discretion
Always as four rak'at, since missed prayers are owed in full
questions.explanation: Missed prayers keep their original form: a prayer missed while traveling is always made up as two rak'at, regardless of whether the person is traveling or resident at the time of قَضَاء.

questions.question: What is the Hanafi position on the خُطْبَة in the Jumu'ah prayer?
options: A nafl act performed before the first adhan
A recommended sunnah that increases reward but does not affect the prayer's validity
A شَرْط (condition) of the Jumu'ah prayer itself
A وَاجِب that makes the prayer deficient but not invalid if omitted
questions.explanation: Per Hanafi fiqh, the خُطْبَة is a شَرْط (condition) of the Jumu'ah prayer — not merely a sunnah — meaning the prayer is invalid without it.

questions.question: Which term describes a city where a traveler intends to stay for 15 or more days?
options: مِصْر
قَضَاء
وَطَن أَصْلِي
وَطَن إِقَامَة
questions.explanation: وَطَن إِقَامَة is the city of intended stay — when a traveler plans to remain there for 15 or more days, that city becomes their وَطَن إِقَامَة and ends their traveler status for prayer purposes.

questions.question: What does جَمْع فِعْلاً mean?
options: Praying two prayers at the exact midpoint between their times
Merging the actual time windows of two prayers into one
Shortening each prayer to two rak'at and performing them back-to-back
Apparent combination by stretching prayer times so they appear adjacent
questions.explanation: جَمْع فِعْلاً (apparent combination) means delaying one prayer to the end of its time and hastening the next to the start of its time, so they appear combined — without actually merging the time windows, which is جَمْع وَقْتًا and disallowed by the Ahnaf.
